result:
task: Lens G, "The tools we chose to glue, not build". For every tool the Gov OS selected, I recorded what is installed and whether it is pinned, measured whether it is used, compared what we built against what the tools already do, checked the gaps against official sources, and recommended what to keep, configure, replace or retire.
status: DONE
work_completed: I inventoried the 23 registry entries, 7 tools that are used but not registered, and S0b2's leftover installs. Status, measured: ACTIVE 18, PASSIVE 3 (openspec, lefthook, superpowers), BROKEN 1 (codebase-memory-mcp through our wrapper), REPLACED 1 (check-jsonschema). Q3 compares 8 built areas with tools, and Q4 maps 8 gaps to mature tools, using 27 official sources read on 2026-10-19. The report has 11 findings (F1 high; F2 to F9 medium; F10 and F11 low) and 10 recommendations, plus a ranked list of the glue that saves the most build. I re-read the whole report from the file after the last edit.
files_changed: only the report. My scratch work (the clone, scripts and outputs) is in `/tmp/gov-os-assessment-G/`. I wrote nothing else, installed nothing, changed no settings and made no commits.
evidence: doctor run from my clone (G-1). Code-graph probe in a bubblewrap sandbox (G-3): the whole-graph edge query is refused at 100k rows, the tool's own per-kind queries and `trace_path` answer, and paging with SKIP inside the query loses rows without an error. Schema probe (G-4): a planted ticket has 7 schema errors and `gov` finds 0; 4 of 558 real records fail their schema. The guard's own refusal function, called on six command strings (G-5). Transcript counts (G-6). Glue size: 15,914 non-blank lines (G-7). The 59-minute close in `close-DAEO-7rr2-3.json`. S0b2's own tool registry for the leftover installs.
tests: none run. No regression, `gov close` or `gov rebuild` (Limits 4). pytest-testmon was not installed or run (Limits 6). CI was not run (Limits 7).
discoveries: 116 commands were refused as "cannot be read" in October, about two thirds of them heredocs. S0b2's language servers, TypeScript and its 1.5 GB Rust toolchain are still installed, although DEC-074 records "rejected tools uninstalled", and W2-19 queues a Rust install (Q-6) when one is already present. Doctor reports openspec as ok although it cannot start on the default Node. `pyproject.toml` pins nothing and leaves out sqlite-vec. Neither the schema fix nor the code-graph fix has an owner: W2-02 may change only the type map, and W2-37's paths leave out `codeintel`. DEC-726 item 1 (a cache keyed on exact hashes) rules out the pytest-testmon option that item 2 asks W2-48 to compare. lefthook 2.2.0 fixes writing an install-time path into AI hook configs; the pinned 2.1.15 does not have that fix. Other sessions wrote files while I worked (Limits 9).
risks: F1, a code-graph fix that pages with SKIP inside the query would drop rows without an error. F2, a misspelt status or class passes the schema check. F3, a worker resumed by hand loses its sandbox. F7, W2-05 and W2-08 can stall on the byte-identical settings file. F9, the code keeps growing with no size review held.
lessons: count transcript hits strictly: a first count of 160 refusals included 42 results that only showed the refusal text, such as reads of the guard's code. Check each citation against what the tool actually returned, not against memory; four web rows and several code ranges were corrected this way. Re-check figures carried across a context compaction: "22 close logs" were really 11 share records, and "origin not recorded" was wrong, since S0b2's registry records those installs.
proposed_decisions: (1) widen the held W2-02's paths to the validator part of `check/schema.py`, and rule on the 4 imported decision records (R2); (2) give the code-graph fix an owner, and make "the code graph answers on this repository" an entry criterion of W2-37 (R1, DEC-803); (3) restate DEC-726 item 1 and W2-48's key requirement as behaviour before W2-48 starts (R6); (4) take DEC-781's "not applicable here" branch for openspec (R10); (5) hold DEC-064's size review now (R9); (6) resume workers only with `gov launch … --resume`, as part of W2-56 and W2-21 (R3); (7) add the missing registry entries and decide S0b2's leftovers before Q-6 is answered (R4); (8) choose a lefthook option for W2-05 after an owner-run measure (R7); (9) in W2-42, put the sandbox first and use one shared tokeniser, with tree-sitter-bash only after a trial (R5).
unresolved: the guard refused reads of the settings files, so lefthook's install and any sandbox block in the project settings were not checked. I did not check whether any hand resume was of a sandboxed worker. testmon's fit rests on its documentation, not a run. Contract v4.2 was not read. In the workbench I opened only the four files named by exact path. The claude.ai Gmail and Google Calendar connectors are attached but not authorised; this session cannot authorise them, so they must be authorised in the claude.ai connector settings and are unavailable until then (this lens did not need them).
recommended_next_action: the owner's decision on the size review (R9). Then the R1, R2 and R6 decisions, before W2-37 starts, W2-02 resumes and W2-48 starts.
